title: The Farther Reaches of Human Nature

contents: Part I, Health and Pathology: Toward a Humanistic Biology; Neurosis as a Failure of Personal Growth; Self-Actualizing and Beyond
Part II, Creativeness: The Creative Attitude; A Holistic Approach to Creativity; Emotional Blocks to Creativity; The Need for Creative People
Part III, Values: Fusions of Facts and Values; Notes on Being-Psychology; Comments from a Symposium on Human Values
Further parts on education, society, transcendence, and metamotivation, assembled from late essays and lectures
Editors' framing by Bertha G. Maslow with Henry Geiger

audiences: Readers tracing self-actualization and the hierarchy of needs to the source
Students of humanistic and transpersonal psychology
Coaches, educators, and leaders drawn to growth-centred views of people
Readers of positive psychology curious about its ancestry

sources.title: Review of The Farther Reaches of Human Nature
sources.author_or_publisher: Wesley Wildman's Religious Experience Resources, Boston University
sources.supports: The posthumous assembly, the concept vocabulary (peak experiences, B-values, B-cognition, Jonah complex), the third-force framing, Maslow's rejection of value-neutral science, and the caution that peak experiences should not be artificially pursued.
sources.limitations: Sympathetic academic review focused on religious-experience themes.
